LIKELY_PHISHING.title: Spotting a phishing email
LIKELY_PHISHING.body_html:
Spotting a phishing email

Phishing messages try to trick you into clicking a malicious link, opening an attachment, or revealing a password. Before acting, ask:

  • Do I recognise the sender?
  • Does the request feel urgent or unusual?
  • Does the link go where it claims?

When in doubt, report the message and verify out-of-band.

BEC_IMPERSONATION.title: Business-email-compromise (BEC)
BEC_IMPERSONATION.body_html:
Business email compromise

BEC attackers impersonate executives or vendors to redirect payments or steal data. Red flags:

  • Urgency around payment changes
  • Reply-to address differs from the sender
  • New banking instructions

Confirm payment changes by phone using a number you already know.

LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN.title: Lookalike domains
LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN.body_html:
Lookalike domains

Attackers register near-miss domains like example-corp.com instead of example.com. Hover over the sender to inspect the full address before replying.

SUSPICIOUS_URL.title: Suspicious links
SUSPICIOUS_URL.body_html:
Suspicious links

Hover before clicking. Watch out for shortened URLs, mismatched display text, and domains you don't recognise. SN360 routes risky links through a safety check.

SUSPICIOUS_ATTACHMENT.title: Suspicious attachments
SUSPICIOUS_ATTACHMENT.body_html:
Suspicious attachments

Don't open attachments you weren't expecting — especially Office docs that ask to enable macros, or .iso/.html files. Verify with the sender first.

FIRST_CONTACT_EXTERNAL.title: First-time external sender
FIRST_CONTACT_EXTERNAL.body_html:
First-time external sender

You haven't received email from this address before. Take a moment to confirm the sender's identity before taking action or sharing information.

ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER_SUSPECTED.title: Possible account takeover
ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER_SUSPECTED.body_html:
Possible account takeover

This sender's behaviour looks different than usual. Their account may be compromised. Avoid replying with sensitive data and confirm via another channel.

VENDOR_COMPROMISE.title: Vendor compromise
VENDOR_COMPROMISE.body_html:
Vendor compromise

A known vendor's account may be impersonated. Re-verify any payment instructions or sensitive requests through a phone number from a prior, trusted record.

CREDENTIAL_HARVESTING.title: Credential harvesting
CREDENTIAL_HARVESTING.body_html:
Credential harvesting

Real services never ask you to confirm a password by clicking a link. If you're unsure, navigate directly to the service in your browser — don't use the email's link.

INVOICE_FRAUD.title: Invoice fraud
INVOICE_FRAUD.body_html:
Invoice fraud

Be cautious of last-minute banking-detail changes, unfamiliar PO numbers, or urgent payment requests. Always verify by calling a known finance contact.

QR_PHISHING.title: QR-code phishing
QR_PHISHING.body_html:
QR-code phishing

Attackers embed malicious URLs in QR codes to bypass link inspection. Don't scan QR codes from unverified emails — open the linked service directly instead.

SCAM_FRAUD.title: Scams and fraud
SCAM_FRAUD.body_html:
Scams and fraud

Promises of money, prizes, romance, or threats demanding payment are classic scam patterns. If it feels too good — or too scary — to be true, it usually is.

AUTH_FAILED.title: Failed sender authentication
AUTH_FAILED.body_html:
Failed sender authentication

The sender's domain failed SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks. The message may be spoofed. Treat any links or requests with extra caution.

INTERNAL_TRUSTED.title: Internal email
INTERNAL_TRUSTED.body_html:
Internal email

This message is from within your organisation. Even so, accounts can be compromised — treat unusual requests with the same care you would for external email.

VENDOR_TRUSTED.title: Trusted vendor
VENDOR_TRUSTED.body_html:
Trusted vendor

This sender is on your tenant's vendor allowlist. SN360 still watches for vendor-compromise patterns — flag anything that looks out of character.

NEWSLETTER.title: Newsletter / bulk email
NEWSLETTER.body_html:
Newsletter / bulk email

Newsletters are usually safe to read but rarely require urgent action. Use the unsubscribe link rather than reporting bulk senders as phishing.
